benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Brent (January contract) settled up 2.3% at $91.40/bbl on 24 Nov (Bloomberg, via Rigzone), partly reversing the prior day's selloff, as reports of fresh Hormuz tanker attacks offset lingering hopes for more Iran diplomacy in thin pre-Thanksgiving trading; week_ago uses the nearest confirmed settlement, 16 Nov.

note: Brent climbed 2.3% to $91.40/bbl and WTI rose 2.4% to $82.05/bbl on 24 Nov, partly reversing the prior day's selloff, as reports of renewed Hormuz tanker attacks offset lingering Iran-diplomacy hopes in thin pre-Thanksgiving trading (Bloomberg, via Rigzone). MarineTraffic data cited by Al Jazeera showed vessels entering and exiting the Gulf fell to 125 in the week of 17-23 Nov from 226 in the week of 1-7 Nov, a roughly 40% drop. TTF, JKM and Henry Hub were little changed from 23 Nov.
